zh.summary: 分清身分、存取權限與工作階段，為十人共用的候選架構寫出存取處的控制及負向情境。
objectives: 為資料讀取與匯出指定伺服器端授權檢查。
將單人原型與未實作的多人安全需求分開記錄。

readingGuide.startingPoint: architecture.md及合成A／B角色卡；不建立真實帳號、不存真實資料。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 architecture.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: architecture.md中獨立的共用版候選控制及負向情境。

sections.heading: 登入後，還需要判斷哪些事？
paragraphs: 這一課最重要的觀念：登入系統，不代表可以使用系統裡的所有功能，也不代表能查看別人的資料。
我們要學會區分三件事情：

1. Authentication（身分驗證）：你是誰？如何證明？
2. Authorization（授權）：你能做什麼？可以存取哪些資料？
3. Session（工作階段）：系統如何在你持續操作時認得你，以及何時讓這個登入狀態失效？
這一節的核心是：從單人軟體變成多人共用系統時，如何避免使用者看到、修改或匯出不屬於自己的資料。

sections.heading: 一、先用生活例子理解三個概念
paragraphs: 假設你走進一家大型醫院，想查看病人的病歷。
1. Authentication：確認身分
醫院要求你刷員工證、輸入密碼或使用其他驗證方式，確認你確實是某位醫師。
解決的是「你是不是你宣稱的那個人？」。
2. Authorization：判斷權限
系統確認你是醫師後，還需要檢查你是否有權查看這位病人的病歷。
解決的是「即使知道你是誰，你有沒有權限做這件事？」。
3. Session：管理持續操作
你登入後，通常不需要每點開一頁就重輸密碼。但當你登出、閒置過久或工作階段失效，就需要重新驗證。
解決的是「如何在多次操作之間安全地維持狀態？」。
把它們整理成一張表：

blocks.caption: 三概念對照
rows: 判斷可否讀取病人甲的病歷
如何維持這次操作狀態？
管理登入後的識別資訊、效期與登出

paragraphs: 注意：醫師並非一定可以看所有病歷，必須依醫院的存取政策、醫療照護關係與適用規範判定。

sections.heading: 二、Authentication：登入只是確認身分
paragraphs: 想像你到銀行櫃檯辦理業務。
行員首先會確認你的身分證件，目的不是決定你可以領多少錢，而是先確認你究竟是誰。
網站登入也是同樣道理。
常見的身分驗證方式包括：

- 密碼：證明你知道某個祕密。
- OTP（一次性密碼）：使用簡訊或驗證器產生的驗證碼。
- Passkey（通行密鑰）：利用密碼學金鑰完成身分驗證，常結合裝置解鎖。
- MFA（多因素驗證）：組合不同類別的驗證因素，提高冒用難度。
例如，你使用帳號與密碼登入公司的文件系統，系統成功確認你是員工 A。
但這只代表：
系統已確認目前提出要求的人，是通過驗證的 A。
它沒有直接代表：

- A 可以查看所有公司的文件。
- A 可以刪除其他人的文件。
- A 可以下載整個客戶資料庫。
這就是為什麼身分驗證與授權必須分開。

sections.heading: 三、Authorization：已經登入，還要確認能不能做這件事
paragraphs: 假設一家保險公司有十位員工，每人負責不同客戶的理賠案件。
員工 A 負責案件 `CASE-101`，員工 B 負責 `CASE-202`。
他們都成功登入，而且都是「理賠專員」。那麼 B 能不能直接查看 A 的案件？
不一定。即使兩個人職稱相同，也不表示可以存取相同的資料。
以下是假設的權限政策：
實際系統可能還有主管複核、案件交接、代理人等規則，但不能因為某人是主管，就自動假設他有權看全部資料。

blocks.heading: 1. 授權真正需要判斷哪些事情？
paragraphs: 可以拆成四個因素：

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜授權判斷的四個因素
blocks.description: 四列是共同參與判斷的因素，不代表先後步驟。

items.title: Context（情境）
items.body: 是否符合時間、案件關係等條件？

paragraphs: 例如，系統需要判斷：
員工 B，現在是否有權匯出 CASE-101？
不是只有判斷「B 是不是理賠專員」。

blocks.heading: 2. 三種常見權限設計
paragraphs: 比較授權依據：角色、屬性或人與資源的關係。

blocks.caption: 三種權限模型
rows: 按各種屬性和條件決定
只有特定部門、符合案件狀態的員工可以核准
按人與資源的關係決定
案件負責人、被指派的複核者可以查看案件

paragraphs: 這三種模型不是非此即彼。大型系統通常需要組合。
例如 RBAC 確定你具有「理賠專員」資格，ReBAC 再判斷你和特定理賠案件的關係。
OWASP 建議採用最小權限（Least Privilege）、預設拒絕（Deny by Default），並針對每一次存取要求檢查權限。

blocks.heading: 3. 為什麼只隱藏按鈕非常危險？
paragraphs: 假設系統提供這兩個 API：

blocks.heading: 讀取與匯出 API
paragraphs: 示例尚未執行，不代表已實作安全控制。
第一個讀取資料，第二個匯出資料。
開發者可能想：「B 不能匯出 A 的案件，那就不要讓 B 看到匯出按鈕。」
問題是，使用者並不一定要透過畫面按鈕才能對伺服器提出請求。
他可以使用其他 HTTP 用戶端要求匯出；如果伺服器沒有檢查權限，資料仍可能外洩。
因此，權限必須落實在真正處理資料的地方。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜安全的資料存取判斷流程
blocks.description: 箭頭代表判斷路徑；失效或無權限即拒絕，不繼續讀取。每個資料入口都要執行檢查：讀取、修改、下載、匯出、API、批次工作。

items.title: 伺服器檢查工作階段
items.body: 失效 → 拒絕；有效 → 檢查案件權限

items.title: 檢查使用者對該案件的權限
items.body: 無權限 → 拒絕且不回傳資料內容；有權限 → 存取資料

items.title: 失效 → 拒絕
items.body: 停止處理，不存取案件資料。

paragraphs: 概念性流程圖。實作時應在每個受保護入口及相應資料存取路徑執行授權控制。
這也解釋了兩種常見的安全問題：
Horizontal Privilege Escalation（水平越權）：B 和 A 同級，但 B 卻能查看 A 的私人資料。
Vertical Privilege Escalation（垂直越權）：一般員工取得原本只有管理員才能使用的功能。

sections.heading: 四、Session：為什麼登入一次，就能連續操作？
paragraphs: 這裡要先理解 HTTP 的特性。
HTTP 本身基本上是 Stateless（無狀態）的，也就是各次請求獨立，協定不會自動記住「這一個請求跟剛才那個請求是不是同一個人」。
那為什麼你登入購物網站後，點開商品、加入購物車、查看訂單，不必每次重輸密碼？
因為網站建立了管理使用者持續互動狀態的機制。

blocks.heading: 1. Session 怎麼運作？
paragraphs: 以常見的伺服器端 Session 為例：

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜瀏覽器與伺服器如何維持工作階段
blocks.description: 兩個角色分工；瀏覽器向伺服器送出 Cookie，伺服器驗證 Session 是否有效。這不是兩個依序執行的狀態。

items.title: 伺服器端概念紀錄（示意）
items.body:
Session ID → 隨機不可預測的識別值
User → A
Created → 建立時間
Expires → 失效時間
Revoked → 是否已撤銷

paragraphs: 流程是：使用者完成身分驗證，伺服器建立 Session，瀏覽器保存其識別資訊，之後提出請求時附上這個識別資訊。伺服器判斷 Session 是否有效，並且仍然需要檢查資料存取權限。
Cookie 是瀏覽器儲存和傳送資訊的機制；Session 是管理持續互動狀態的概念；Token 是可用於識別或授權的憑證形式。三者相關，但不能畫上等號。

blocks.heading: 2. Session 必須有生命週期
paragraphs: 假設你登入網路銀行後離開電腦。
如果登入狀態永久有效，就可能讓其他使用那臺電腦的人繼續操作你的帳戶。
所以安全設計通常需要：

blocks.caption: 工作階段生命週期
rows: 一段時間沒有活動，工作階段失效
即使持續使用，到達最長期限仍須失效或重新驗證
使用者主動登出，使相關工作階段失效
系統主動撤銷工作階段或憑證
遇到敏感操作或風險事件，要求再次驗證

paragraphs: 這些不是統一設定為幾分鐘就適合所有系統。銀行轉帳、購物網站、醫療系統，需要依照風險和使用情境設計不同政策。OWASP 也指出，工作階段識別資訊若遭竊取，可能導致 Session Hijacking（工作階段劫持）。
常見的 Cookie 保護屬性有 `Secure`、`HttpOnly`、`SameSite`。它們分別協助限制傳輸方式、JavaScript 存取以及跨網站請求時的 Cookie 傳送行為，但仍不能取代完整的授權與其他安全防護。
還有一個容易搞混的觀念：Session 可以存在於未登入的情境。 例如匿名訪客選擇了網站語言或暫存購物車，系統也可能維持一個匿名工作階段。

sections.heading: 五、換成不同行業，再比較一次
paragraphs: 比較各產業時，依序辨認身分確認、資源操作權限及持續互動狀態。

blocks.caption: 跨產業比較
rows: 能否查詢該帳戶、執行轉帳
維持及限制網銀登入狀態
教師能否修改某門課的成績
管理教務系統工作階段
能否查看某筆訂單、申請退款
維持會員操作與購物車
能否修改特定設備參數
控制操作台的有效登入
確認使用者或服務身分
能否呼叫工具、讀取文件、執行動作
管理對話或工具執行中的安全狀態

paragraphs: 其中，AI Agent 特別值得留意。
假設公司開發了一個可以搜尋文件的 AI Agent。員工 B 要求：「幫我整理 A 所負責客戶的全部合約。」
Agent 即使正確識別了 B，也不能因此直接搜尋所有文件。
授權控制必須延伸到實際的文件檢索、資料庫查詢、工具呼叫和匯出操作。單純在 System Prompt 寫上「不可讀取未授權資料」，不足以成為可靠的存取控制。

sections.heading: 六、教材中的 Streamlit：有 Session State，不代表有安全登入
paragraphs: 這是本節容易產生誤解的地方。
教材使用 Streamlit 原型。Streamlit 提供 `st.session_state`，可以保存某個使用者工作階段內的互動狀態，例如選擇的檔案、畫面欄位或操作結果。
但它本身並不代表已經完成正式的身分驗證或資料授權。
另外，Streamlit 也提供 `st.login()`、`st.user` 和 `st.logout()`，可以整合 OpenID Connect（OIDC）身分驗證。這仍然不會自動完成你的業務資料授權。
因此要分清楚：

blocks.caption: Streamlit 能力界線
rows: 應用程式保存了工作階段的互動狀態
可建立身分驗證流程，需正確配置
應用程式自己的權限規則
判斷特定使用者是否能操作特定資源
需要額外檢查失效、撤銷、重新驗證等要求是否滿足

paragraphs: 不能因為畫面能記住使用者代號，就宣稱系統已經支援十個人安全共用。

sections.heading: 七、怎麼把這堂課變成實際的軟體規格？
paragraphs: 原始教材要求把「十人共用版」的候選安全控制寫進 `architecture.md`，而且要明確保留尚未實作的狀態。
以下是一個可以參考的版本：

blocks.heading: 候選安全規格
paragraphs: 示例尚未執行，不代表已實作安全控制。
blocks.code:
## 多人共用版安全設計（候選規格）

狀態：待實作／待驗證

### 1. Authentication
- 使用者身分來源：待決定
- 登入及驗證方式：待決定

### 2. Authorization
- 每筆案件有明確的授權關係
- 讀取、修改、匯出分別檢查
- 伺服器端執行授權檢查
- 未明確允許的存取預設拒絕
- 拒絕時不得回傳未授權資料內容

### 3. Session
- 工作階段建立與效期：待設計
- 閒置逾時與登出：待設計
- 權限撤回後的處理：待設計
- 敏感操作重新驗證：待設計

### 4. 負向測試
- B 讀取 A 的私人案件 → 拒絕
- B 匯出 A 的私人案件 → 拒絕
- 未登入讀取私人案件 → 拒絕
- Session 失效後存取 → 拒絕
- 權限撤回後再次存取 → 拒絕

以上均尚未執行，不得標記測試通過。

## Shared-version security design (candidate specification)

Status: not implemented / not verified

### 1. Authentication
- User identity source: undecided
- Login and verification method: undecided

### 2. Authorization
- Each case has an explicit authorization relationship
- Check reads, changes and exports separately
- Enforce authorization server-side
- Deny access unless explicitly allowed
- Denial must return no unauthorized record content

### 3. Session
- Session creation and lifetime: to design
- Idle expiry and logout: to design
- Handling withdrawn permissions: to design
- Reauthentication for sensitive actions: to design

### 4. Negative tests
- B reads A's private case → deny
- B exports A's private case → deny
- Unauthenticated access to a private case → deny
- Access after session invalidation → deny
- Access after permission withdrawal → deny

None of these tests has been executed. Do not mark them as passing.

paragraphs: 這份規格最重要的目的不是讓文件看起來完整，而是讓開發團隊清楚知道：哪裡需要檢查、什麼情況必須拒絕、哪些安全能力尚未驗證。

sections.heading: 八、最後的理解檢核
paragraphs: 假設一家律師事務所建立了一個案件管理系統，三位使用者分別是 A 律師、B 律師及 C 行政人員。
A 負責案件 X，B 負責案件 Y，C 負責部分案件的行政協助。三個人都成功登入系統。
系統必須在真正存取資源的地方，判斷現在是否允許這個人執行這個動作；這是從個人原型走向安全多人系統的門檻。

exercise.environment: architecture.md及合成A／B角色卡；不建立真實帳號、不存真實資料。
steps: 分別寫出身分、授權與工作階段問題，標明目前原型未實作。
畫共用版候選資料路徑，在伺服器讀取與匯出處標記授權檢查，寫B讀A資料的負向情境。
列未登入、工作階段失效與權限撤回的待確認行為，記負責角色與待驗證據，不填虛構通過。
exercise.expected: architecture.md中獨立的共用版候選控制及負向情境。
exercise.check: 能分開登入與授權，不把session_state或按鈕隱藏當隔離；沒有宣稱本機原型已支援多人安全。
exercise.cleanup: 只用合成代號，保留未實作狀態；不輸入或分享實際cookie、token與密碼。

en.summary: Separate identity, access permissions and sessions, then specify access-point controls and negative scenarios for a candidate ten-user architecture.
objectives: Distinguish authentication, authorization and session responsibilities.
Specify server-side authorization checks for reading and exporting data.
Record the single-user prototype separately from unimplemented multiuser security needs.

readingGuide.goal: Distinguish authentication, authorization and session responsibilities.
readingGuide.startingPoint: architecture.md and synthetic A/B role cards; create no real accounts and store no real data.
readingGuide.route: Read the situation and principles, compare examples, then expand architecture.md and review the checks.
readingGuide.output: A separate candidate shared-version control and negative-scenario section in architecture.md.

sections.heading: What must be checked after login?
paragraphs: Logging in does not grant access to every feature or to other people's data.
Distinguish three responsibilities:

1. Authentication: Who are you, and how do you prove it?
2. Authorization: What may you do, and which data may you access?
3. Session: How does the system recognize continuing interactions, and when does that state become invalid?
When a single-user application becomes a shared system, these responsibilities help prevent users from viewing, changing or exporting data that is not theirs.

sections.heading: 1. Understand the three concepts through an everyday example
paragraphs: Imagine entering a large hospital to view a patient's medical record.
1. Authentication: establish identity
The hospital asks you to present an employee badge, enter a password or use another verification method to establish that you are a particular doctor.
This answers: “Are you the person you claim to be?”
2. Authorization: decide permission
After identifying you as a doctor, the system must still check whether you may view this patient's record.
This answers: “Knowing who you are, are you allowed to do this?”
3. Session: manage continuing interaction
After logging in, you normally do not re-enter your password for every page. Logging out, remaining idle too long or session invalidation may require authentication again.
This answers: “How can state be maintained safely across multiple actions?”
Compare the responsibilities in a table:

blocks.caption: Three responsibilities
rows: Establish that this is Dr. Wang
Decide whether you may read patient A's record
How is this interaction state maintained?
Manage identification information, expiry and logout

paragraphs: A doctor does not automatically have access to every medical record. Access depends on hospital policy, the care relationship and applicable requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Authentication: login establishes identity
paragraphs: Imagine conducting business at a bank counter.
The clerk first checks identification to establish who you are. This step does not decide how much you may withdraw.
Website login follows the same distinction.
Common authentication methods include:

- Password: demonstrate knowledge of a secret.
- OTP (one-time password): use a code delivered by text message or generated by an authenticator.
- Passkey: use cryptographic keys, often together with device unlocking.
- MFA (multi-factor authentication): combine different categories of authentication factors to make impersonation harder.
For example, an account and password establish that the user of a company document system is employee A.
The result means:
The system has established that the current requester is authenticated as A.
It does not establish that:

- A may view every company document.
- A may delete other people's documents.
- A may download the entire customer database.
Authentication and authorization therefore need separate decisions.

sections.heading: 3. Authorization: check this action even after login
paragraphs: Suppose an insurance company has ten employees, each responsible for different customers' claims.
Employee A handles `CASE-101`; employee B handles `CASE-202`.
Both are logged in and both have the role “claims specialist.” May B view A's case directly?
Not necessarily. Sharing a job title does not imply sharing access to the same records.
Consider this hypothetical policy:
Actual systems may also have supervisor review, case handover or delegation rules. Do not assume a supervisor automatically has access to everything.

blocks.heading: 1. What must an authorization decision consider?
paragraphs: Separate four factors:

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Four factors in an authorization decision
blocks.description: The four rows contribute to one decision; they are not sequential steps.

items.title: Context
items.body: Are time, case relationship and other conditions satisfied?

paragraphs: For example, the system must decide:
May employee B export CASE-101 now?
Checking only whether B is a claims specialist is insufficient.

blocks.heading: 2. Three common access-control models
paragraphs: Compare the basis for permission: roles, attributes or relationships between people and resources.

blocks.caption: Three access-control models
rows: Accounting staff may use expense reporting
Only employees in a specified department may approve a case in the required state
Decide using relationships between people and resources
The case owner and assigned reviewer may view the case

paragraphs: These models can be combined. Large systems often need a combination.
For example, RBAC establishes eligibility as a claims specialist, while ReBAC checks the relationship to the particular claim.
OWASP recommends least privilege, deny by default and authorization checks on every access request.

blocks.heading: 3. Why is hiding a button insufficient?
paragraphs: Suppose the system exposes two APIs:

blocks.heading: Read and export APIs
paragraphs: This example has not been executed and does not establish implemented controls.
The first reads data; the second exports it.
A developer might hide the export button from B because B cannot export A's case.
However, a user can send requests without pressing a button in the interface.
Another HTTP client can request the export directly. If the server does not check permission, the data may still leak.
Enforce authorization where data is actually processed.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | A safe data-access decision flow
blocks.description: Arrows indicate decision paths. An invalid session or denied permission stops access. Check every data entry point: reads, changes, downloads, exports, APIs and batch jobs.

items.title: Server checks session
items.body: Invalid → deny; valid → check case permission

items.title: Check permission for this case
items.body: No permission → deny without record content; permission → access data

paragraphs: This is a conceptual decision flow. Implement checks at each protected entry point and its data-access path.
Two common problems follow from missing checks:
Horizontal privilege escalation: B has the same organizational level as A but can view A's private data.
Vertical privilege escalation: an ordinary employee gains access to a function reserved for administrators.

sections.heading: 4. Sessions: why can one login support continuing actions?
paragraphs: Start with HTTP's behavior.
HTTP is stateless: individual requests are independent, and the protocol does not automatically remember whether the current request comes from the same person as the preceding request.
Why can you log in to a shopping site, open products, add items to a cart and view orders without entering a password each time?
The site supplies a mechanism to manage state across interactions.

blocks.heading: 1. How does a session work?
paragraphs: Consider a common server-side session:

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Browser and server session responsibilities
blocks.description: Two roles work together. The browser sends a cookie to the server, which checks session validity. These are not two sequential states.

items.title: Conceptual server-side record
items.body:
Session ID → random unpredictable identifier
User → A
Created → creation time
Expires → expiry time
Revoked → revocation status

paragraphs: After successful authentication, the server creates a session and the browser retains its identifying information. Later requests carry that information. The server checks session validity and still checks authorization for the requested data.

A cookie is a browser storage and transmission mechanism. A session is a way to manage continuing interaction state. A token is a form of credential that can support identification or authorization. They are related concepts with different responsibilities.

blocks.heading: 2. Sessions need a lifecycle
paragraphs: Suppose you log in to online banking and leave the computer.
If the login remains valid forever, another person using that computer may continue operating your account.
Security design commonly needs these controls:

blocks.caption: Session lifecycle
rows: Invalidate the session after a period of inactivity
Expire or require reauthentication at the maximum lifetime even if activity continues
Invalidate relevant sessions when the user signs out
Let the system invalidate sessions or credentials
Require authentication again for sensitive actions or risk events

paragraphs: One timeout value does not suit every system. Bank transfers, shopping sites and healthcare systems need policies based on their risks and use contexts. OWASP also explains that stolen session identification information can enable session hijacking.

Common cookie protections include `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite`. They help restrict transport, JavaScript access and cookie sending with cross-site requests. They still need authorization and other security controls alongside them.
Sessions can also exist before login. For example, an anonymous session may retain a language preference or temporary shopping cart.

sections.heading: 5. Compare the responsibilities across industries
paragraphs: Across industries, identify identity verification, resource permissions and continuing interaction state separately.

blocks.caption: Industry comparison
rows: Decide access to an account or a transfer
Maintain and limit online-banking login state
Decide whether a teacher may change grades for a course
Decide access to an order or refund request
Maintain member interactions and cart state
Decide whether an operator may change particular equipment parameters
Decide tool calls, document access and permitted actions
Manage security state during conversation or tool execution

paragraphs: Consider an AI agent in particular.
A company builds a document-search agent. Employee B asks: “Summarize all contracts for the customers handled by A.”
Even if the agent correctly identifies B, it cannot infer permission to search all documents.

Authorization must extend to document retrieval, database queries, tool calls and exports. A system-prompt instruction saying “do not read unauthorized data” is insufficient as an access-control boundary.

sections.heading: 6. Streamlit: session state does not establish secure login
paragraphs: This distinction can be misunderstood.
The course uses a Streamlit prototype. `st.session_state` retains interaction state for a user session, such as the selected file, form fields or results.
Using it does not establish production authentication or authorization for business data.
Streamlit also provides `st.login()`, `st.user` and `st.logout()` for OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication. These functions still do not automatically implement business-data authorization.
Distinguish the following capabilities:

blocks.caption: Streamlit capability boundaries
rows: The application retains interaction state within a session
An authentication flow can be established with correct configuration
Decide whether a particular user may operate on a particular resource
Requires additional checks of expiry, revocation and reauthentication requirements

paragraphs: A screen remembering a user code does not demonstrate safe sharing by ten users.

sections.heading: 7. Turn the lesson into a software specification
paragraphs: Record candidate controls for the shared ten-user version in `architecture.md`, retaining their unimplemented status.
Use this reference template:

blocks.heading: Candidate security specification
paragraphs: This example has not been executed and does not establish implemented controls.
blocks.code:
## 多人共用版安全設計（候選規格）

狀態：待實作／待驗證

### 1. Authentication
- 使用者身分來源：待決定
- 登入及驗證方式：待決定

### 2. Authorization
- 每筆案件有明確的授權關係
- 讀取、修改、匯出分別檢查
- 伺服器端執行授權檢查
- 未明確允許的存取預設拒絕
- 拒絕時不得回傳未授權資料內容

### 3. Session
- 工作階段建立與效期：待設計
- 閒置逾時與登出：待設計
- 權限撤回後的處理：待設計
- 敏感操作重新驗證：待設計

### 4. 負向測試
- B 讀取 A 的私人案件 → 拒絕
- B 匯出 A 的私人案件 → 拒絕
- 未登入讀取私人案件 → 拒絕
- Session 失效後存取 → 拒絕
- 權限撤回後再次存取 → 拒絕

以上均尚未執行，不得標記測試通過。

## Shared-version security design (candidate specification)

Status: not implemented / not verified

### 1. Authentication
- User identity source: undecided
- Login and verification method: undecided

### 2. Authorization
- Each case has an explicit authorization relationship
- Check reads, changes and exports separately
- Enforce authorization server-side
- Deny access unless explicitly allowed
- Denial must return no unauthorized record content

### 3. Session
- Session creation and lifetime: to design
- Idle expiry and logout: to design
- Handling withdrawn permissions: to design
- Reauthentication for sensitive actions: to design

### 4. Negative tests
- B reads A's private case → deny
- B exports A's private case → deny
- Unauthenticated access to a private case → deny
- Access after session invalidation → deny
- Access after permission withdrawal → deny

None of these tests has been executed. Do not mark them as passing.

paragraphs: The specification tells the team where checks belong, which conditions must deny access and which security capabilities remain unverified.

sections.heading: 8. Check your understanding
paragraphs: A law firm has three users: lawyer A, lawyer B and administrator C.
A handles case X, B handles case Y, and C assists with administrative work on selected cases. All three are logged in.
At the actual resource-access point, decide whether this person may perform this action now. This is a necessary step from a personal prototype toward a secure shared system.

exercise.environment: architecture.md and synthetic A/B role cards; create no real accounts and store no real data.
steps: List identity, authorization and session questions separately, marking each formal control absent from the current prototype.
Draw the candidate shared data path; mark server-side authorization at read/export and specify B requesting A-only data.
List undecided unauthenticated, expired-session and revoked-permission behavior, with responsible roles and missing evidence; invent no passing results.
exercise.expected: A separate candidate shared-version control and negative-scenario section in architecture.md.
exercise.check: Separate login from authorization. Neither session_state nor hidden buttons establish isolation or multiuser security.
exercise.cleanup: Use synthetic labels and retain unimplemented status. Enter or share no actual cookies, tokens or passwords.

zh.prompt: B 律師將案件網址中的 Y 改成 X，伺服器卻直接回傳 X 的內容。最主要是哪一類安全問題？
rationales: B 已登入；此情境的主要問題是資源授權。
伺服器沒有確認 B 是否有權查看案件 X，造成水平越權。
調短逾時不會補上對案件 X 的授權檢查。
Cookie 格式不能決定 B 是否有權查看 X。

en.prompt: B changes Y to X in the case URL and the server returns X. What is the principal security problem?
rationales: B is logged in; resource authorization is the primary issue.
The server failed to check permission for case X, enabling horizontal privilege escalation.
A shorter timeout cannot supply the missing case authorization check.
Cookie format does not establish permission for case X.

zh.prompt: C 行政人員已登入系統，卻不能下載某份文件。這一定代表系統有問題嗎？
options: 一定有，登入就應允許下載
不一定，可能是正確的授權限制
一定是 HTTPS 沒有啟用
rationales: 登入只確認身分，不授予所有下載權限。
必須依 C 與該文件的授權關係及下載動作判斷。
僅從無法下載，無法推定 Session 已失效。
無法下載不能直接證明 HTTPS 狀態。

en.prompt: C is logged in but cannot download a document. Does this necessarily indicate a fault?
options: No; it may be correct authorization enforcement
It must mean the session expired
It must mean HTTPS is disabled
rationales: Login establishes identity, not every download permission.
Check C’s relationship to the document and the requested download action.
A denied download alone does not establish an expired session.
A denied download does not establish HTTPS status.

zh.prompt: A 離職後，原本建立的有效工作階段仍可繼續讀取案件。你最應優先檢查哪個設計？
rationales: 配色不會撤銷既有工作階段。
檔名不會阻止已撤權者存取。
檢查離職事件是否撤回權限、失效相關工作階段，並在存取時重新核對。
排版不會實作撤權或工作階段失效。

en.prompt: After A leaves the firm, an existing session can still read cases. Which design should you inspect first?
rationales: Colors do not revoke existing sessions.
File names do not prevent access after permission withdrawal.
Check permission withdrawal, invalidation of relevant sessions and fresh checks at access time.
Responsive layout does not implement revocation or session invalidation.
